summary.text: A 23-year-old man, a university student with a 3-month history of depressive symptoms and no prior psychiatric care, was brought to the emergency department approximately 36 hours after intentionally ingesting more than 30 tablets of amlodipine 10 mg and an unknown quantity of diclofenac 50 mg in a suicide attempt, after which he vomited 2 to 3 times.

At triage blood pressure was 85/36 mmHg, pulse 66 beats/min and oxygen saturation 86% on room air. On examination he was lethargic but fully oriented with GCS 15/15. Initial laboratory evaluation showed WBC 27.1 × 10³/µL and creatinine 2.8 mg/dL with normal electrolytes, an electrocardiogram showed bradyarrhythmia with idioventricular rhythm, and no arterial blood gas was performed.

He received intravenous crystalloids, calcium gluconate 2 g IV, an epinephrine infusion and atropine with minimal effect, then HIET. During the first 48 hours he developed acute kidney injury and non-cardiogenic pulmonary edema with bilateral pleural effusions and received antibiotics for suspected sepsis. On hospital day 3 he required intubation and suffered a cardiac arrest during induction, with ROSC after 3 CPR cycles.

In the ICU he needed continued vasopressors, high-dose insulin, hydrocortisone and loop diuretics, was extubated on day 7 of ventilation, and had left leg cellulitis. By hospital day 15 he was alert and stable; he was transferred to the medical ward and later discharged with complete neurologic recovery, then referred to psychiatry, where major depressive disorder was diagnosed and interpersonal therapy commenced.
